items.claim: The stated ground for declining a cut at 15:19 is byte-false: the divine reply is not already underway there, because 15:15-18 is the prophet's own voice, so the verse-initial koh-amar does carry a change of speaking mouth; two ketiv/qere notes inside the span are also undisclosed.
items.evidence: The reply opening at 15:11 runs to 15:14; 15:15 turns to the prophet addressing Yahweh, אַתָּ֧ה יָדַ֣עְתָּ יְהוָ֗ה זָכְרֵ֤נִי וּפָקְדֵ֨נִי֙ (oshb:Jer.15.15, byte tier), a vocative divine name followed by first-person-suffixed imperative forms, and the complaint continues to 15:18, הָי֨וֹ תִֽהְיֶ֥ה לִי֙ כְּמ֣וֹ אַכְזָ֔ב (oshb:Jer.15.18, byte tier). Both witnesses render 15:15-18 in the prophet's voice. So לָכֵ֞ן כֹּֽה אָמַ֣ר יְהוָ֗ה (oshb:Jer.15.19, byte tier) resumes divine speech after four verses of complaint: the mouth carrying the formula changes at 15:19, which makes it a live internal seam candidate rather than the non-event asserted, and the rival is set aside on a premise the bytes contradict. Verified and not challenged: the alef-lexeme digit is right, a token-bound sweep returning 8 verses book-wide including 13:27 and 15:10, matching the staged count object; and parashah disclosure is complete and correctly typed (setumah at MT 15:10, 15:14, 15:16, 15:17, 15:18; petuchah at MT 15:21, the two types kept distinct). Undisclosed: the ketiv/qere inventory records one note at MT 15:11, שרותך שֵֽׁרִיתִ֖יךָ (oshb:Jer.15.11, byte tier), in the very verse cited as the reply's onset, and one at MT 15:16, דבריך דְבָֽרְךָ֙ (oshb:Jer.15.16, byte tier).

items.claim: Two stated grounds are byte-contested - the koh-amar at 16:5 heads the mourning prohibition itself rather than a rationale at 16:6-7, and the span is not addressed to one hearer named in it - and the parashah-position statement is wrong for the mark at MT 16:4.
items.evidence: Verified: 16:1 is one of the twenty-one verse-initial word-event onsets of the vayehi debar-YHWH shape in the staged frame inventory, and MT 16:9 is a member of the 32-verse full divine-title stack; both splices re-collate at byte tier. Contested: כִּֽי כֹ֣ה אָמַ֣ר יְהוָ֗ה אַל תָּבוֹא֙ בֵּ֣ית מַרְזֵ֔חַ (oshb:Jer.16.5, byte tier) puts the formula and the prohibition in one verse, so at that site the koh-amar introduces a fresh command rather than explaining a command just given, and 16:6-7 carries no koh-amar at all, so the pairing stated for the mourning command mislocates its formula. The prophet's name occurs in no verse of chapters 15, 16 or 17 (token-bound sweep, both attested spellings, 0 verses in each chapter), and 16:9 addresses a second-person plural audience, לְעֵינֵיכֶ֖ם וּבִֽימֵיכֶ֑ם (oshb:Jer.16.9, byte tier), not the second-person-singular hearer of 16:2, 16:5 and 16:8, so the one-named-hearer ground fails on both counts. The setumah keyed to MT 16:4 stands after that verse, between the marriage command-and-rationale block of 16:2-4 and the mourning command at 16:5, that is between two prohibitions; only the MT 16:8 mark falls inside a command-and-rationale pair, so the claim that both interior breaks fall inside a prohibition holds for one of the two.

items.evidence: לֹא תָב֖וֹא (oshb:Jer.16.8, byte tier) and כִּ֤י תַגִּיד֙ (oshb:Jer.16.10, byte tier) are both second-person-singular verbs directed at the prophet, so no frame-level addressee change occurs at 16:10; the plural address in this stretch stands at 16:9, before the onset rather than at it. The clause typed a discourse-frame imperative is וְאָמַרְתָּ֣ (oshb:Jer.16.11, byte tier), a waw-prefixed second-person-singular suffix-conjugation form, not an imperative form; both witnesses render it as a consequent directive statement, and the byte exemplars of that signal class at 4:5 and 10:1 are true imperatives. No morphology layer is staged, so the label rests on the pointing, which does not support it. The same conditional-plus-answer construction stands mid-unit at 15:2, וְאָמַרְתָּ֨ אֲלֵיהֶ֜ם (oshb:Jer.15.2, byte tier), so the shape alone is not a row-opening seam here.
